title: Q3 Bank Earnings Kick Off Season (Goldman, JPMorgan, Citi, BofA $1.2B Fine)
summary: Gotrade News - Goldman Sachs (GS) reported third-quarter earnings of $17.01 per share on Tuesday, October 13, beating Wall Street estimates on a 72% jump
body_markdown:
CEO Jamie Dimon warned that "large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates" are shifting "under the surface," as reported by the AP. The same report noted that the Federal Reserve raised interest rates last month, a backdrop that featured in the[big banks' Q3 earnings kickoff](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/big-banks-kick-off-q3-earnings/) .


## Citigroup Q3 Profit Rises 40%, Wells Fargo Beats


Citigroup's third-quarter profit rose 40% from a year earlier and beat expectations, with investment banking and wealth management revenue higher and credit card profits flat, per the AP.


Investing.com reported Citi EPS of $2.85 against a $2.65 consensus and revenue of $23.85 billion against $23.72 billion expected. Wells Fargo earned $5.95 billion, or $1.87 a share, which the AP said beat forecasts.


## Bank of America Hit With $1.2 Billion Treasury Fine


A day before its own results,[Bank of America (BAC)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/bac/) was ordered to pay a $1.2 billion penalty that the Treasury Department called the third-largest in its history, according to[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/corporations/bank-america-sanctions-violations-penalty-rcna603251) .


The total includes $750 million from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the largest fine that regulator has ever levied, per NBC.


Treasury said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions on time and "admits that it willfully violated" the Bank Secrecy Act, as reported by NBC News.


A separate OFAC settlement covers 475 apparent sanctions violations. Bank of America said "financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right," and it is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings before 7 a.m. ET on Wednesday.


## GS, JPM and C Stock Reaction and Analyst Commentary


Goldman shares rose 1.9% and JPMorgan gained 0.8% in early trading on Tuesday, while Citigroup slipped 0.7% and Wells Fargo fell 1.5%, according to the AP.


In a[Q3 review](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4953934-goldman-sachs-q3-the-business-deserves-a-premium-the-stock-already-has-one) on Seeking Alpha, analyst Kenio Fontes noted that the EPS and 18.7%[return on equity](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-equity-in-finance/) reflect some cyclical and one-off factors, including incentive fees, and flagged limited margin for error if ROE falls below 15%.
